nodes.summary: Always restore pac auth to Test (index [2]) after any Prod/Stage deploy

nodes.label: Authentication Methods
nodes.summary: How Claude and scripts actually authenticate to DCFG services
nodes.detail: Multiple auth surfaces: pac CLI (deploy ops), Core.ps1 (Dataverse API), Playwright (portal Web API + E2E tests), MSAL device-code (Graph/SharePoint). Each has constraints and failure modes.

nodes.label: Core.ps1 pattern
nodes.summary: PowerShell Dataverse auth via Core.ps1 — the reliable path for API scripts
nodes.detail: Location: C:/DCFG/PowerApps-Samples/dataverse/webapi/PS/Core.ps1. Usage: `Connect $orgUrl` → populates `$baseHeaders` globally → use with `Invoke-RestMethod`. OrgUrl MUST have trailing slash. Token is short-lived — re-acquire when switching environments in long scripts. Do NOT use Az module / Connect-AzAccount; az CLI is not installed on this machine.

nodes.label: pac CLI auth
nodes.summary: pac auth list / select / pages upload — for SPA deploy only, not Dataverse API tokens
nodes.detail: `pac auth list` shows all profiles with active index (*). `pac auth select --index N` switches. Used for: `pac pages upload-code-site`, `pac pages download`. Cannot be used to acquire bearer tokens for API calls — `pac auth token` does not exist in pac CLI v2.4.1.

nodes.label: Playwright portal auth
nodes.summary: Playwright is the proven path for portal Web API calls — reads /_api/ using session cookies from Windows Hello login
nodes.detail: Pattern: write a .spec.ts, navigate to portal, pause for Windows Hello, use `page.evaluate(() => fetch('/_api/...'))` for GETs. For POST/PATCH/DELETE: get CSRF token via `window.shell.getTokenDeferred()` — raw fetch('/') HTML scraping returns wrong/expired token. Auth state saved to nora/auth-state.json (Stage) or nora/prod-auth-state.json (Prod) and reused across runs.

nodes.label: Windows Hello auth
nodes.summary: All DCFG staff use Windows Hello (biometric/PIN) — no passwords to automate
nodes.detail: Playwright must use manual-pause pattern: navigate to portal → console.log instructions → waitForURL with 120s timeout for user to complete Windows Hello. Never fill email/password fields. .env does NOT need TEST_USER_PASSWORD. After first manual login, auth state is saved and reused. KMSI ('Stay signed in?') page from Microsoft blocks auth flow — click Yes or handle inline.

nodes.label: MSAL device-code (Graph/SharePoint)
nodes.summary: Graph tokens via MSAL device-code flow for SharePoint access — separate from Dataverse token
nodes.detail: Script at C:/DCFG/tools/path-probe/graph-auth.py. Scope: `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default`. Dataverse bearer token cannot access SharePoint — confirmed 401. Must acquire a separate Graph token for any SharePoint read/write. MSAL device-code flow is the only proven mechanism here.

nodes.label: Token Management
nodes.summary: Dataverse tokens, SharePoint/Graph tokens, and CSRF tokens are three separate concerns
nodes.detail: Three distinct token surfaces: (1) Dataverse bearer token via Core.ps1 Connect — short-lived, re-acquire per environment. (2) Graph/SharePoint token via MSAL device-code — separate acquisition. (3) Power Pages CSRF token for portal Web API writes — from `window.shell.getTokenDeferred()` only.

nodes.label: Dataverse bearer token
nodes.summary: Acquired via Core.ps1 Connect — short-lived, fails cross-env if not re-acquired
nodes.detail: Core.ps1 Connect populates $baseHeaders including Authorization: Bearer. Short-lived — for scripts that touch multiple environments, call Connect again with the new orgUrl before making calls to that env. Cannot be used for SharePoint — 401 on any SharePoint endpoint.

nodes.label: Graph / SharePoint token
nodes.summary: MSAL device-code with graph.microsoft.com/.default scope — completely separate from Dataverse token
nodes.detail: Acquired by C:/DCFG/tools/path-probe/graph-auth.py. Required for any SharePoint library operation (DCFG_Templates, DCFG_Outputs). Dataverse token used on SharePoint endpoints returns 401 with no redirect. These two tokens are completely non-interchangeable.

nodes.label: Power Pages CSRF token
nodes.summary: Required for portal Web API writes — get from window.shell.getTokenDeferred() only
nodes.detail: All POST/PATCH/DELETE to /_api/ need __RequestVerificationToken header. Must come from `window.shell.getTokenDeferred()` inside a page.evaluate() Playwright call. Scraping the token from page HTML (hidden input or fetch('/') parse) returns wrong/expired tokens and causes 403. Token can expire mid-session — invalidate and re-fetch on 401/403.

nodes.label: Entra Configuration
nodes.summary: Entra ID app registration that backs Power Pages portal authentication
nodes.detail: App: Decades Management System. Client ID: 327ac710-2d2a-4912-a5ee-9b7f51ee7a7b. Object ID: 47b371c4-b13b-44d2-863e-74a7e80caad1. Tenant ID: 71ccf1ec-8b0a-4419-9a45-a617aa1a66d6. Single-tenant (My organization only).

nodes.label: Redirect URI safety rule
nodes.summary: Only ADD redirect URIs — never remove existing ones
nodes.detail: The Entra app has 1 SPA redirect URI as of 2026-03-18. Unknown services may depend on it. When provisioning a new portal environment (e.g., holding.powerappsportals.com for Stage needs /signin-openid), ADD only. Removing any existing URI risks breaking portal auth silently — portal auth can break without obvious error messages.

nodes.label: Portal auth silent failure
nodes.summary: Portal Entra auth can break silently — fix by disable/re-enable in Power Pages admin
nodes.detail: If portal login stops working without obvious error: go to Power Pages admin → External auth → disable then re-enable. Then redeploy SPA and clear cache. There is no visible error in the portal UI when Entra auth is misconfigured — users just get stuck at the login page.

nodes.label: Portal auth state files
nodes.summary: Auth state saved per environment — Stage at nora/auth-state.json, Prod at nora/prod-auth-state.json
nodes.detail: Playwright saves authenticated session after first Windows Hello login. Stage: nora/auth-state.json with playwright.config.ts (baseURL: holding.powerappsportals.com). Prod: nora/prod-auth-state.json with playwright-prod.config.ts (baseURL: dmms1.powerappsportals.com). Reused for all subsequent test runs without re-authenticating.

nodes.label: KMSI page trap
nodes.summary: Microsoft 'Stay signed in?' page blocks Playwright auth flow — must click Yes or handle explicitly
nodes.detail: After Windows Hello login completes, Microsoft shows 'Keep Me Signed In?' interstitial. Playwright waitForURL targeting the portal URL will time out if this page is not handled. Add explicit KMSI page detection and click Yes, or use a broad enough waitForURL pattern that catches the KMSI URL too.

nodes.label: pac CLI
nodes.summary: pac CLI v2.4.1 — primary tool for SPA deploy and portal manifest management
nodes.detail: Version: v2.4.1. Key commands: `pac auth list`, `pac auth select --index N`, `pac pages upload-code-site --rootPath . --compiledPath dist`, `pac pages download --path . --webSiteId {id} --modelVersion Enhanced`. Deploy always from spa/dcfg-shell/ after `npm run build`.

nodes.label: pac auth select safety gate
nodes.summary: Always run pac auth list, verify * is on the correct index, before any pac pages command
nodes.detail: On 2026-04-05, pac auth was silently on Prod when Test was intended — SPA deployed to Prod without authorization. Protocol: (1) `pac auth list` — check which index has *. (2) Confirm it matches the intended target by verifying the org URL. (3) If wrong, `pac auth select --index N` then re-verify. (4) Never assume a prior `pac auth select` succeeded.

nodes.label: pac auth token does not exist
nodes.summary: `pac auth token` is not a valid command in pac CLI v2.4.1 — do not attempt
nodes.detail: This command was considered as a way to acquire a Dataverse bearer token from the CLI session. It does not exist in this version. Reaching for it wastes time. Use Core.ps1 Connect for Dataverse API tokens instead.

nodes.label: Orphan powerpagesites after solution import
nodes.summary: Solution import copies powerpagesites records — pac targets the wrong site when duplicates exist
nodes.detail: When importing DCFGSystemTest to a new environment, ALL powerpagesites records from the solution are copied. Result: the real site plus stage/test orphans. pac pages upload-code-site --siteName matches the wrong site. Manifest.yml locks to whichever site PAC first resolved. Fix: delete ALL orphan powerpagesites records (keep only the real one), delete local manifest yml, then run `pac pages download --webSiteId {correct-id}` to re-initialize before uploading.

nodes.label: pac pages download --modelVersion Enhanced
nodes.summary: EDM sites require -mv Enhanced flag for pac pages download
nodes.detail: Enhanced Data Model (EDM) sites need `--modelVersion Enhanced` flag when running `pac pages download`. Without it the download either fails or produces the wrong file structure. `pac pages upload` equivalent also works for pushing content. Site ID for Stage: a150bd53-7fbc-423d-a1ad-dd653ab4c435.

nodes.label: Auth Traps
nodes.summary: Known dead ends and failure modes in the DCFG auth surface
nodes.detail: Collected traps that have burned time. Each has a verified workaround or confirmed dead-end status. Read before attempting any auth approach for the first time.

nodes.label: Connect-CrmOnline popup trap
nodes.summary: Connect-CrmOnline (Microsoft.Xrm.Data.PowerShell) opens a GUI credential popup — blocks all automation
nodes.detail: Calling `Connect-CrmOnline` in any script context triggers a Windows GUI credential dialog. Since auth is Windows Hello (no passwords), this dialog cannot be completed programmatically. It hangs automation indefinitely. Never use Connect-CrmOnline — use Core.ps1 → Connect $orgUrl instead.

nodes.label: curl.exe blocked
nodes.summary: curl.exe is blocked by endpoint security — use Invoke-RestMethod in pwsh instead
nodes.detail: Endpoint security on this machine blocks curl.exe entirely. No workaround. Always use `Invoke-RestMethod` inside a pwsh process. This applies to any HTTP call from scripts — Dataverse API, Graph API, any REST endpoint. Never attempt curl.exe.

nodes.label: az CLI not installed
nodes.summary: az CLI is not installed — do not attempt Get-AzAccessToken or any az command
nodes.detail: The Az PowerShell module and az CLI are both absent from this machine. Any script referencing `Get-AzAccessToken`, `Connect-AzAccount`, or `az account get-access-token` will fail immediately. The engineering journal section 7 shows an old auth pattern using Az — that pattern is dead on this machine.

nodes.label: Bash $ eats pwsh strings
nodes.summary: Bash eats $ in pwsh command strings — write .ps1 files and use pwsh -File instead
nodes.detail: When invoking `pwsh -Command "..."` from bash, bash interpolates `$` variables, mangling OData `$filter=...` and `$select=...` query params into empty strings. The Dataverse API returns 'query parameter not supported' with no hint about the cause. Fix: write the PowerShell to a .ps1 file and invoke with `pwsh -NoProfile -File path.ps1`. Same applies to nested regex escapes — `\\` becomes `\` in the bash → pwsh pipeline.

nodes.label: Shifted PAC indices trap
nodes.summary: PAC indices in CLAUDE.md are stale — indices shifted when profiles were re-created
nodes.detail: CLAUDE.md documents [1]=Test, [2]=Stage, [3]=Prod, [6]=Portal. Actual as of 2026-04-12: [1]=Prod, [2]=Test, [3]=Stage, [4]=Portal. Any hardcoded index in a plan or script must be verified with `pac auth list` before execution. The indices can shift again — always verify the org URL, not just the number.

nodes.label: Cross-env URL contamination in flows
nodes.summary: Solution import leaks Test/Stage org URLs into Prod flow clientdata — watch for this
nodes.detail: Three Prod flows (cert_alert, onboarding_init, send_email) contain Test/Stage org URLs in their clientdata — introduced by solution import rather than being authored in-place. If a flow behaves correctly in one env but fails in Prod, inspect the clientdata for hardcoded org URLs that don't match. Fix: update flow clientdata to use Prod URLs or make the URLs config-driven.

nodes.label: Prod Environment Setup Auth Steps
nodes.summary: Auth-specific steps in the proven Prod provisioning order
nodes.detail: From the proven 12-step Prod setup checklist: step 4 = create web roles (DCFG_Admin with authenticatedusersrole=true), step 7 = add Entra ID redirect URI (add-only, never remove), step 8 = `pac pages download --webSiteId {correct-id}` to initialize manifest, step 9 = `npm run build && pac pages upload-code-site`. Full checklist in reference_engineering_journal.md section 19.

nodes.label: Open Questions
nodes.summary: Unresolved auth questions and areas of uncertainty
nodes.detail: Items that need clarification or further investigation before being treated as settled.

nodes.label: Existing SPA redirect URI purpose unknown
nodes.summary: The existing SPA redirect URI in the Entra app registration serves an unknown service — identity unknown
nodes.detail: As of 2026-03-18, the Entra app has 1 SPA redirect URI. The reference file notes it must NOT be removed because unknown services may depend on it. The exact service or portal it serves has not been documented. Before any Entra app changes, confirm what this URI serves.

nodes.label: feedback_no_crm_online_module.md partially stale

nodes.detail: feedback_no_crm_online_module.md (19 days old) says Playwright is the only reliable Dataverse API path. reference_lessons_2026_04_16.md (2 days old) contradicts this — Core.ps1 + pwsh also works reliably. The newer evidence should take precedence. Both paths are currently valid. The old memory file should be updated to reflect Core.ps1 as an equally valid option.

nodes.label: HAL Service Principal
nodes.summary: DCFG-HAL-Automation SP enables non-interactive Dataverse access on Test and Stage
nodes.detail: Client ID: 58529ef1-0170-4fa0-81d9-187da60426f8. Client credentials flow (client_secret grant). Application users created in both Test (770cb2bb) and Stage (241905d2) with System Administrator role. Verified via WhoAmI. Config in hal/references/hal-auth.json. Temp scripts cleaned. pac auth create failed (admin API 403) but direct token+REST works.

nodes.label: SP Auth Pattern — client_credentials
nodes.summary: POST to /oauth2/v2.0/token with client_credentials grant, scope={orgUrl}/.default
nodes.detail: Token endpoint: https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/token. Body: grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, scope={orgUrl}/.default. Returns access_token valid 3600s. Use in Authorization: Bearer header for Dataverse API calls.

nodes.label: pac auth create fails for SP — use direct REST
nodes.summary: pac auth create with --applicationId succeeds at token but 403s on admin API verification — profile not saved
nodes.detail: pac admin create-service-principal and pac auth create both try to call the Power Platform admin API after authenticating. The SP doesn't have admin API access, so it 403s and the profile isn't saved. Workaround: use direct OAuth2 token + Invoke-RestMethod for all SP operations. pac CLI stays on user profiles.

nodes.label: App user creation via Dataverse API
nodes.summary: POST systemusers with applicationid + businessunitid@odata.bind creates application user without admin portal
nodes.detail: Using existing user auth (Core.ps1), POST to /api/data/v9.2/systemusers with {applicationid, fullname, businessunitid@odata.bind}. Then assign role via /systemuserroles_association/$ref. Avoids needing Power Platform admin center GUI entirely.
